title: WLB-LLM: Workload-Balanced 4D Parallelism for Large Language Model Training
problem: Large language model training requires parallelization across multiple dimensions (data, tensor, pipeline, sequence), but existing strategies suffer from load imbalance and inefficient resource utilization.
motivation: Balanced parallelism across 4D (data/tensor/pipeline/sequence) improves GPU utilization and reduces training time for billion-scale LLMs.
method: Large language model training distributes work across four dimensions: splitting data samples (data parallelism), dividing network weights (tensor parallelism), breaking computation into stages (pipeline parallelism), and splitting text sequences (sequence parallelism). WLB-LLM continuously rebalances load across these dimensions based on your hardware layout and the cost of moving data between processors, rather than using a fixed strategy. This keeps all processors equally busy instead of having some wait idle for others to finish.
key_novelty: It dynamically adjusts how the four parallelism dimensions (data, tensor, pipeline, sequence) share the workload, based on actual conditions instead of a fixed strategy.
contributions: Adaptive parallelism strategy based on hardware and workload
Improved GPU utilization and reduced training time for large LLMs

metrics.other: Training throughput and GPU utilization improvement

limitations: Overhead of dynamic balancing and applicability to emerging model architectures require further investigation.
